extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, applicants, agents, examiners, and legal practitioners dealing with UK Patents/Designs/Trade Marks
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing filing, content, amendment, acceptance, enforcement, and associated filings for Patents (with related rules for Designs and Trade Marks) under the Patents, Designs, and Trade Marks Act and accompanying rules. Covers specification sufficiency, form requirements, timings, amendments, enforcement pleadings, and appeals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application for a Patent — formal requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must be in the English language; contain a declaration; be signed by the applicant (or made by agent if authorised in writing); require a £1 stamp (and additional stamp if declared before a Commissioner); be accompanied by a specification; contain an address; be properly numbered and may be sent by post; must contain one invention (procedures where more than one invention stated); referred to an Examiner; Comptroller may require amendment after Examiner's report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms and signatures: agent may sign other communications but cannot sign application itself except where authorised; numbering, form of application, and where it may be sent by post are prescribed; applicant may be heard if Comptroller requires amendment; subject to appeal to law officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete specification — sufficiency requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete specification must (1) be intelligible to ordinary workmen possessing some skill; (2) not omit a material part of a process nor contain misleading or ambiguous statements; (3) distinguish what is new from what is old (except universally known matters or parts not forming part of the invention); (4) disclose the most beneficial way of exercising the invention, referring to materials used including cheapest and specifying improvements; (5) not vary from the provisional specification; (6) end with a claim which must not exceed the title and ought to be limited to one invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners report on preparedness and variance from provisional specification; reports are not conclusive; Comptroller may require amendment after hearing; claims exceeding title or multiple-invention issues give rise to specific procedures; omission or variance cases discussed in authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for filing and acceptance of complete specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete specification may be left with the application or within nine months of application; if not left within nine months the application is deemed abandoned. Acceptance of complete specification must be within twelve months (unless appeal pending); acceptance gives provisional protection and is advertised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees apply (e.g., £3 stamp for complete specification). Acceptance is advertised in the Official Journal and specifications and drawings become open to inspection on advertisement; effects on infringement and scope depend on publication and acceptance timings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of specification — clerical and substantial amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Clerical errors may be corrected by the Comptroller. Substantial amendments require leave (Comptroller or court/judge) and must not enlarge the invention; leave obtained after application, advertisement, and potential opposition and evidence on hearing. Amendments while legal proceedings pending require a court's leave. Amendments are not retrospective except in certain good-faith circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure: form of request for leave, fee, advertisement of request, opposition procedure, evidence on hearing, appeal to law officer. Leave once given is conclusive except for fraud. New specification may need to be lodged; amendment may be allowed after adverse judgment as to validity (with limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings — requirements and practice for patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings required when necessary to explain the invention; originals and copy drawings must meet size rules; absence of a scale is an imperfection; drawings may explain ambiguities and are reported on by Examiners. For costly drawings, only two copies may be required in some cases; copies for the Illustrated Journal have special requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules and instructions prescribe size, number of copies, lodging times (copies must be lodged at least one week before hearing), and when tracings/photographs/specimens may substitute. Examiner may report on sufficiency of drawings; practice notes set out handling and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action for infringement — prerequisites, pleadings, and evidence limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: An action for infringement cannot be brought until the Patent is granted and not for acts committed prior to publication of the complete specification (with limited exceptions). Trials are without jury unless leave granted; assessors may be called. Statements of claim must be accompanied by particulars of breaches and should state the part of the specification and parts of the accused machine alleged to infringe. No evidence is allowed of infringements not particularised unless by leave; particulars may be amended by leave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costs of actions tied to certification of reasonable proof; amendments of particulars/defences by leave only; account and damages remedies and elections; procedural forms and timing rules apply; courts may order inspection and call assessors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Particulars of defence — prior user and prior publication requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Particulars of defence must be delivered with the statement of defence and must specify prior user (names of prior users, extent of use), particulars of prior publications (books specified with pages and dates, numbers of specifications), allegations of fraud or misrepresentation, and objections that the specification fails to distinguish old from new or fails to set out the best method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generality of particulars cannot be objected to at trial; first inventor need not be named; certain formulaic phrases (e.g., 'and others') have effects that are discussed; particulars required to be sufficiently specific and may be amended by leave.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller powers and discretionary procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comptroller refers applications and specifications to Examiners, may require amendments, advertises acceptances, hears oppositions, causes patents to be sealed and registers them, may enlarge time for fees, hear applications for amendment, refuse grants if contrary to law or morality, and correct clerical errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise of discretionary power requires that the applicant be heard before adverse action; notice forms for hearing and requests to be heard are prescribed; decisions of Comptroller are subject to appeal to Law Officer, Board of Trade, or Court as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals — procedure, grounds and time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals lie (depending on the subject) to the Law Officer (e.g., as to amendments, refusals), to the Board of Trade (e.g., as to Designs and Trade Mark registration), and to the Court. Notices of appeal, statements of case, and evidence rules apply; some appeals must be given within specified short periods (e.g., 14 days for certain law officer appeals, one month for Board of Trade appeals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms of notice and statements are prescribed; appeals may be referred to Court by the Board of Trade; practice on appeal (evidence, hearing) is regulated and fees may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims — structure and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Every complete specification must end with a claim. A claim must not exceed the title; claims should be limited to one invention in the complete specification (though multiple-invention claims on application have special procedures). A claim of more than one invention in specification is not ground to invalidate a patent at trial in some circumstances but is handled procedurally on application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comptroller and Examiners consider whether title indicates subject matter; rules exist for when multiple inventions appear and for rectifying or amending claims; changes to claims are subject to scrutiny and possible restriction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance and publication — effects and inspection
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptance of an application or complete specification is advertised (e.g., in the Official Journal), after which applications including specifications and drawings are open to inspection. Acceptance gives provisional protection and affects the ability to sue for past acts (publication timing affects what acts may be relied upon).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance must occur within statutory time limits; reports of Examiners are not published; admissions and publications have defined legal consequences for infringement and evidence; copies of specifications/drawings are kept for sale and distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of particulars of breaches or objections — by leave only
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment of particulars of breaches or particulars of objections in infringement proceedings may be made only by leave of the court or judge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leave may be given with conditions; application for leave follows prescribed procedure and may be influenced by timing and fairness to the other party.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment and registration of assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignments of patents, designs, and trade marks should be registered (entered on the register) with prescribed forms; assignments may be for particular places; assignments of trade marks are assignable only with the goodwill (except series rules), and rules exist for registration and forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forms and fees apply; entries on the register serve as evidence; special rules exist for assignments before application, assignments on bankruptcy (vesting in trustee), and for registration by corporate names or representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete specification amendments during litigation — special leave and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment of a specification during legal proceedings requires leave of the Court or a judge; copy of the order must be left with the application; trial may be postponed; amendment may be given in evidence but is not retrospective; fees and advertisement of amendment apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comptroller's leave is different from Court leave; amendment during action affects damages and other remedies and may be refused in cases of fraud or if it would prejudice third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designs — registration criteria and filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A Design is entitled to registration if it is new or original and has not been published in the United Kingdom. Applications must state the nature of the design, the class of goods, be accompanied by a sketch and three drawings (one sketch allowed initially), and conform to size and form rules. Acceptance results in a certificate of registration; refusal triggers a hearing and appeal to the Board of Trade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings may be refused if unsuitable; tracings, photographs, or specimens/representations may be accepted instead of drawings; class selection and potential multiple-class registration are important; Comptroller decides doubts as to class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright in Designs — scope, duration and cessation
rubrics_metrics.description: Copyright in designs is restricted to the classes for which the design is registered, limited in duration (e.g., five years), and ceases if exact specimens or representations are not furnished before delivery of articles on sale or if articles are not marked with prescribed marks (unless proprietor took proper marking steps). Use abroad without UK use within six months may cause cessation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificate of copyright may be required; penalties and remedies for piracy of designs are set out; inspection and action for infringement or penalties depend on these conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade mark application — formal and evidentiary requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications to register a Trade Mark must specify the class of goods, include a representation of the mark (with translation for foreign characters), provide particulars for special goods (e.g., metals used, invoice name for cotton goods), be signed by applicant/agent/officer, be accompanied by additional representations or specimens (number depends on class), and may be sent by post. Comptroller may require further representations or specimens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advertised in Trades Marks Journal; acceptance not effective until specified time after advertisement (e.g., two months); fees payable upon registration and registration must be within statutory periods (e.g., 12 months) unless delay excused; woodblocks/electrotypes may be demanded and not returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusive user of a Trade Mark — evidential effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusive user of a registered trade mark is prima facie evidence of a right to the mark and becomes conclusive evidence after five years' registration/user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This affects remedies and enforcement; conflicts between earlier users and registrants are resolved by Court with reference to evidence and potentially special cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enlargement of time for payments and consequences on remedies
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comptroller may enlarge times for paying Patent fees or taking other prescribed proceedings (conditions apply, not to exceed three months). Acts done during enlarged time can affect remedies — e.g., courts may refuse damages for infringements committed during enlarged time for payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application for enlargement requires form and fee; conditions for granting enlargement are prescribed; effect on remedies (damages vs. account) is specifically addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified and sealed copies and evidentiary value
rubrics_metrics.description: Certified and sealed copies of entries in registers and documents in the Patent Office may be obtained (fees apply) and are receivable in evidence. Some exceptions and transmittals (e.g., to Edinburgh, Dublin, Isle of Man) apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certificates of the Comptroller for use in legal proceedings are also receivable as evidence; specific rules exist for obtaining copies of designs and trade mark proceedings; certified copies of specifications/drawings have prescribed processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibition of inventions and publication consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventions may be exhibited before grant but only at industrial or international exhibitions certified by the Board of Trade; publication of description during exhibitions is addressed and may affect novelty/publication considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board of Trade certifies exhibitions; rules limit where and how inventions may be exhibited without prejudicing patentability; details of timing and evidence of exhibition are relevant to later proceedings.
